profile.headline: Machine Learning Engineer @ Amazon | Former Google, Snapchat, Adobe ML
profile.summary:
Github: github.com/catherinelee274 · X: x.com/cat_eye_on 

ML engineer passionate about pushing the frontier of AI. I work on recommendations and ranking systems, with research interests in LLMs, post-training, alignment, and mechanistic interpretability. Previously at Google, Lamini AI (Series A), Snapchat ML, Adobe ML.

I love open source — I've contributed to HuggingFace TRL and Cohere's multilingual safety work. I love connecting with fellow ML researchers and anyone building at the frontier — let's chat about post-training, alignment techniques, or the latest in ML research :)

honors.description:
Achieved 2nd Place at HackHers.ai 2023 — a competitive AI hackathon with projects evaluated by industry experts from Adept AI (now Amazon AGI), DeepMind, and Anthropic.

Built a Virtual Try-On system using Stable Diffusion and Dreambooth finetuning. Users upload a selfie and a clothing item; the app generates a realistic image of the user wearing the outfit. Features a Next.js frontend and Django REST API backend.

Stack: Stable Diffusion, Dreambooth, PyTorch, LoRA, BLIP captioning, Next.js, Django, TypeScript.

honors.title: LA Hacks 2020 Winner — place.it (Urban Planning Analytics)
honors.description:
Winner at LA Hacks 2020 with place.it — a data-driven urban planning tool that helps city planners, architects, and everyday citizens understand the environmental and social impact of constructing new buildings in Los Angeles.

Users place proposed buildings on a 3D map of LA; place.it then calculates an overall impact score across 6 dimensions: carbon emissions, land valuation, crime rate, parking requirements, transit score, and tree loss. ML models (scikit-learn, R²=0.7 for carbon emissions) trained on real LA city datasets power the ratings.

Stack: Python, scikit-learn, Flask, React, Node.js, Google Maps API, Estated API, SpotCrime API, Los Angeles open datasets.

Devpost: https://devpost.com/software/place-it-n9tq5b

projects.title: MaxRL – Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (Hugging Face TRL)
projects.description:
Open source contribution to Hugging Face TRL adding MaxRL (Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning) as a novel post-training objective for LLMs.

MaxRL bridges traditional RL (REINFORCE/GRPO) with maximum likelihood training using p-normalization to concentrate learning signal on harder examples. Key results vs. GRPO:
• Up to 20× test-time scaling efficiency gains
• Better pass@k diversity retention — resists "solution collapse" during extended training
• Pareto-dominates GRPO across all tested benchmarks

Based on arXiv:2602.02710. PR: github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/5026

projects.title: LLaVA Alignment: Preference Finetuning for Vision Language Models
projects.description:
Explored and compared multiple preference alignment algorithms applied to LLaVA (Large Language and Vision Assistant), a 7B multimodal model. Implemented and benchmarked 5 alignment methods on the RLAIF-V preference dataset:

• DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
• CPO (Contrastive Preference Optimization)
• IPO (Identity Preference Optimization)
• KTO (Kahneman-Tversky Optimization)
• ORPO (Odds Ratio Preference Optimization)

Training pipeline used LoRA (PEFT) on all-linear layers with bf16, gradient checkpointing, and accelerate for multi-GPU support. Goal: understand how different alignment objectives affect multimodal instruction-following quality and reduce hallucinations in vision-language models.

Stack: PyTorch, HuggingFace TRL, LLaVA-1.5-7B, PEFT/LoRA, Accelerate.
